Professional work / 3Cloud

Making complex
systems work.

Production engineering with .NET, React, and Azure. Three pieces of work, from the problem to what changed.

01 / Knowledge, connected

The right answer starts
with the right sources.

The problem
Engineering knowledge was spread across documentation that needed to be searchable.
My contribution
Led architecture and delivery of an Azure RAG knowledge assistant, using Azure OpenAI, AI Search, .NET, and React.
The outcome
A documentation-search platform with monitoring and alerts for production support.

Engineering knowledge assistant / An illustration of retrieval and supporting sources.

02 / Work, in motion

Let the queue
carry the work.

The problem
A serialized replication path constrained how work moved through the system.
My contribution
Replaced that path with asynchronous messaging through Azure Service Bus.
The outcome
Used Application Insights to trace throughput and verify delivery through the new flow.

Asynchronous data replication / An illustrative queue, not a throughput benchmark.

03 / Time, returned

More than 11 hours.
Every day.

The problem
Payment workflows required repeated manual work.
My contribution
Automated those workflows, including a microservice integrated with a bank.
The outcome
Removed more than 11 hours of manual work per day.

Payment automation / An abstract view of the workflow, without client data.

How it works

TERRA

Procedural planet explorer

Terrain streams through Web Workers as a quadtree of patches. Rivers, towns, weather, and seasons come from deterministic generation. Custom shaders handle clouds, oceans, ice, and lava.

Open TERRASource

NACRE

Liquid sculpture studio

WebGPU compute simulates particles. A density field turns them into a continuous surface. Frozen regions keep exact anchors while the rest of the liquid moves.

Open NACRE

PELAGIC

Interactive ocean life

Fixed-step simulations drive tentacles, schooling, feeding, and obstacle avoidance. Instanced fish, procedural anatomy, and translucent shaders run in WebGL with adaptive resolution.

Open PELAGIC
